A store page that answers with a redirect to a foreign host makes the scraping Chrome request and load that foreign page (with the scraping profile's cookies for it) before open_page's final-URL check raises NavigationPolicyError; the call then returns transport_down and nothing from that page. The CDP simulator's S6 records the foreign request (status 200) in both browser paths (2026-11-17). Stopping the request itself would need network interception of main-document requests (Fetch domain or Playwright routing), which the transport does not have. The v2.10.0 notes and changelog say "answers with an error and returns nothing", not "never leaves".

The added S5 case covers a signal-held HTTP 403 self-reload while a public DNS call waits under a configured 20 s bound; it does not prove retained handoff semantics. Inspected current browser_handoff.read_with_handoff disables retention in headless mode, and its headed lease worker returns the challenged payload for a later explicit same-operation call rather than waiting for the challenge to clear. The existing simulator requires real headless Chrome; changing only its HEADLESS setting would fake this precondition. No product hook or headed-launch contract change was added. Whether a real retained challenge can satisfy the plan's waiting-call requirement is unproven, not a runtime-confirmed defect or xfail.

The added S10 case externally closes an actual transport-owned target after a successful read, then bounds the next public search. Inspected open_page always creates fresh targets; the first returned context is held alive solely so the test can close its exact target without suppressing cleanup. This is not loss of a target reused by a retained handoff. The real headless simulator disables that distinct reuse path, so retained-target discard/crash between same-operation handoff calls remains unproven. No product hook, fake reuse or HEADLESS-setting spoof was added.
